entries.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
entries.description: As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.

entries.title: How we contain Claude across products
entries.description: As agents grow more capable, so does their potential blast radius. The engineering question is how to cap it. Here’s what we’ve learned building containment for claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork.

entries.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
entries.description: We traced recent reports of Claude Code quality issues to three separate changes. Here's what happened and what we're changing.

entries.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
entries.description: Harnesses encode assumptions that go stale as models improve. Managed Agents—our hosted service for long-horizon agent work—is built around interfaces that stay stable as harnesses change.

entries.title: How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
entries.description: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts. We built classifiers to automate some decisions, increasing safety while reducing approval fatigue. Here's what it catches, and what it misses.

entries.title: Harness design for long-running application development
entries.description: Harness design is key to performance at the frontier of agentic coding. Here's how we pushed Claude further in frontend design and long-running autonomous software engineering.

entries.title: Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6’s BrowseComp performance
entries.description: Evaluating Opus 4.6 on BrowseComp, we found cases where the model recognized the test, then found and decrypted answers to it—raising questions about eval integrity in web-enabled environments.

entries.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
entries.description: Nicholas Carlini, a researcher on our Safeguards team, explains how he tasked 16 agents with writing a Rust-based C compiler, from scratch, capable of compiling the Linux kernel.

entries.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
entries.description: Agentic coding benchmarks are often treated as precise measurements of relative model capability. However, we’ve found that infrastructure configuration alone can produce meaningful differences in the scores.

entries.title: Designing AI-resistant technical evaluations
entries.description: What we learned from three iterations of a performance engineering take-home that Claude keeps beating.

entries.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
entries.description: Guidance on how to design more rigorous and useful evals for agents across a range of agent architectures and use cases in real-world deployment.

entries.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
entries.description: We developed a two-fold solution to enable the Claude Agent SDK to work effectively across many context windows: an initializer agent that sets up the environment on the first run, and a coding agent that is tasked with making incremental progress in every session while leaving clear artifacts for the next session.

entries.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
entries.description: We’ve added three new beta features that let Claude discover, learn, and execute tools dynamically. Here’s how they work.

entries.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
entries.description: Claude is powerful, but real work requires procedural knowledge and organizational context. Introducing Agent Skills, a new way to build specialized agents using files and folders.

entries.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
entries.description: We explore the emerging art of context engineering and offer a refined mental model for building steerable, effective agents.

entries.title: A postmortem of three recent issues
entries.description: A technical report on three bugs that intermittently degraded responses from Claude. Below we explain what happened, why it took time to fix, and what we're changing.

entries.description: In this post, we describe our most effective techniques for improving performance in a variety of agentic AI systems.
